method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of all prose, stepwise replay of all 14 encoded tableaux and their line references, exercise-count comparison, and exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Three worked propositional tableau constructions, checkmark discipline across open branches, branching-rule order, repeated rule application, an alternative construction order and three exercise sets containing 24 signed-formula problems.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The first example starts a tableau for (A and B) implies A with the false-signed target. False conditional adds true A-and-B and false A. A checkmark may be written only after the corresponding rule has been applied on every open branch. True conjunction then adds true A and true B; true A conflicts with false A, closing the sole branch and hence the tableau.
samples.checks: The false-conditional and true-conjunction signs, line references 1–4, checked markers and close marker are exact. The Marathi retains at-most-one applicable rule for a signed formula and the every-open-branch qualification for checkmarks.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The second example starts with the false sign of (not A or B) implying (A implies B). False conditional yields true disjunction and false inner conditional. True disjunction branches. Applying false conditional on both branches adds true A and false B to each. The right branch closes on B; true negation on the left adds false A and closes that branch.
samples.checks: All five successive tableau encodings preserve branch order, truth signs, rule labels, line numbers and checked/close flags. The order-independence claim is limited by the requirement to apply each corresponding rule in every branch.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The third example begins with two assumptions and demonstrates several branching rules. True disjunction creates A and B-and-C branches; false conjunction splits each into false A-or-B and false A-or-C branches. False disjunction expands each relevant branch, closing the A branches. True conjunction then supplies B and C and closes the remaining branches. A second closed tableau applies the same rules in a different order.
samples.checks: All eight tableaux in this example are source-identical. The prose retains simultaneous application on all relevant branches, the optional visual downward move of a repeated result, the two remaining open branches, and equivalence of the alternative application order.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The three problem sets ask for closed tableaux for 4, 12 and 8 listed signed-formula collections respectively.
samples.checks: All 24 exercise items, their order, signs, parentheses and connectives are byte-preserved; only the repeated instruction was translated.

source_observations: No source correction was required in this unit.
The checkmark convention is explicitly a construction aid rather than part of formal tableau syntax.
The unit contains 14 oltableau environments and 24 exercise items in both source and target.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The established tableau, signed-formula, tree and branch vocabulary remains open to expert correction where exact specialist Marathi evidence is sparse.
The dense branching layouts will receive page-level visual inspection after the complete Tableaux chapter enters a cumulative reader.
